operationalization: Compare Her/Hes reporter period and amplitude in presomitic mesoderm cultured as isolated cells versus as groups, and measure whether grafted cells adopt the host phase or keep their own. Loss of oscillation only in isolation, and phase-locking after grafting, would support the collective claim; persistent single-cell oscillation or failure to entrain would refute it.
obstacles: The dissociation, mutant-graft, and phase-entrainment results come from different labs and species and are not one downloadable time-series table.
Culture density, substrate mechanics, and Notch coupling can mimic a requirement for collectivity.
Chick and zebrafish are thinner in the published imaging record than mouse explants.
rationale: Independent mouse, zebrafish, and human pluripotent-stem-cell studies have published the collective-oscillation and entrainment results, so a restricted version of the claim can be checked by compiling those measurements. Raw fluorescence traces and graft coordinates are mostly supplementary movies rather than a public analysis-ready archive, and no single deposit covers zebrafish, chick, and mouse together. Harmonizing those sources is a months-long curation job, which is why this is only partly resolvable.

operationalization: In the Xenopus neural plate, record regional membrane voltage and the same embryos' brain-marker expression under two perturbations: one that changes absolute voltage while preserving the spatial contrast, and one that flattens the contrast. Expression should track the contrast if the claim is right, and absolute voltage if it is wrong.
obstacles: Public frog transcriptomes after depolarization do not include a matched arm that holds the spatial voltage difference constant.
Voltage images and regional in situ results remain in the original papers rather than a public deposit.
The contrast-versus-absolute design has not been independently replicated with open raw files.
rationale: The decision criterion is a standard physiological contrast, so the claim is operational. The experiments that report it do not have deposited paired voltage maps and spatial expression matrices, and bulk depolarization profiles cannot separate a difference code from an absolute-voltage code. Checking the claim as stated requires those paired measurements, which are not publicly analyzable now.

operationalization: A memory assay could score retained detail against retained behavioral relevance, but the claim is that salience-not-fidelity is the best description across cells to societies, and no single pattern of errors would establish that this description is the right one.
obstacles: Salience is defined by what later matters to an agent, so the measure presupposes the framing under test.
Generalization, abstraction, and ordinary forgetting all produce the same loss of detail.
rationale: The statement is a proposed perspective on memory, not a measurement claim. Experiments can show that some memories keep a useful relationship while dropping specifics, and the same outcomes are already described as generalization or retrieval failure. Nothing in existing data would decide that salience is the correct cross-scale account.

operationalization: The persistence paradox is a philosophical tension about identity through change. No biological variable distinguishes continuous adaptive confabulation as its resolution from other accounts of development and lineage continuity.
obstacles: Identity through change is not a measured variable.
Any observed physiological change can be narrated as confabulation or as ordinary turnover.
rationale: This is a conceptual answer to a paradox about what makes an individual or a lineage persist. Molecular, developmental, and phylogenetic records describe change, but they do not contain a result that would confirm or refute confabulation as the resolution. The claim has no empirical decision criterion.

operationalization: Treating a memory trace as a minimally agential participant in its own reinterpretation does not specify an observation that would differ from ordinary dynamics of an excitable medium.
obstacles: The claim is explicitly a speculation about how to see memories.
Agency of a pattern is not separable from the dynamics of the medium that carries it.
rationale: The text presents this as a way memories could be seen on a processual view of mind. No measurement of neural, cellular, or network activity distinguishes an agential memory from a pattern being transformed by the system that stores it. The claim is not an empirical proposition that current data could settle.

operationalization: Remapping of stored information onto a new context can be measured in particular systems, but success or failure of remapping would not show that this capacity is what binds parts into a Self.
obstacles: Self is not given an operational boundary distinct from physiological or informational coupling.
The claim quantifies over every scale, from cells to organisms.
rationale: Mnemonic improvisation is offered as one kind of cognitive glue that reifies Selves. Coupling, shared dynamics, and information flow are non-cognitive descriptions of the same multi-scale organization, and no public observation picks the glue account out from those rivals. The proposal stays conceptual.

operationalization: Train a specific cue-outcome association in a caterpillar, then after metamorphosis test that same cue against a generalized food cue and against novel cues. Survival of only a generalized mapping would support the claim; retained response to the specific trained cue would refute the claim that specific caterpillar memories do not carry over.
obstacles: The main open behavioral study is odor-shock retention in Manduca, not a leaves-to-food remapping test.
Trial-level choices are in the paper, not a public behavioral repository.
Very few holometabolous species have been tested through metamorphosis.
rationale: Retention of a learned association through metamorphosis is a published, quantitative behavioral result, and that result can speak to whether specific memories survive. The further claim that recall generalizes and remaps, illustrated as leaves becoming food, is not what those assays measured, and the scores are not in a reusable dataset. Existing papers can test part of the statement and leave the remapping clause open.

operationalization: Transfer and odor-seeking experiments can show that a stored trace is incomplete without later interpretation, but both a prompt model and an encoding model predict context-sensitive readout.
obstacles: Prompt versus engram is a description of the same encode-and-decode process.
The cited frog and Aplysia transfer cases do not uniquely favor one description.
rationale: The claim is that engrams are better understood as prompts, with intelligence located in encoding and decoding. Specificity, generalization, and context dependence are expected on both that reading and a standard encoding-plus-retrieval reading. No existing measurement separates the two, so the contrast is not empirically resolvable.

operationalization: Apply the same monensin regimen to tadpole tail amputations and froglet hindlimb amputations and score the identity of the regenerate. Site-appropriate structures, and no tail-from-leg or leg-from-tail outcomes, would support the claim; swapped or nonspecific structures would refute it.
obstacles: Tail regeneration indices are published from one group and are not a deposited animal-level table.
The froglet leg series is not an independent public replication with raw counts.
Monensin also changes sodium, pH, and cell stress, so structure identity has to be scored, not merely whether anything regrows.
rationale: The anatomical contrast is straightforward to score, and published tail experiments already report regeneration indices after a brief monensin treatment. Those numbers, and the corresponding leg results, are not a public dataset an outside group can reanalyze, and they have not been compiled from independent replications. Resolving the location-specific claim needs the paired wound-site data.

operationalization: In polyploid newt kidneys, measure tubule diameter against ploidy, cell size, and cells per cross-section, and record whether the largest cells form a tubule by bending around themselves. Conserved diameter with falling cell number would support the anatomical claim; diameter scaling with cell size would refute it.
obstacles: The measurements are mid-twentieth-century histology tables, not a modern repository.
Cytoskeletal bending versus cell-cell signalling is inferred from cell geometry, not from molecular markers.
The record is limited to salamander kidney tubules.
rationale: Cell size, cell number, and tubule diameter were measured across ploidy series and can still be compiled from those papers, which covers the anatomical half of the claim for newts. The further statement that the tissue switches from cell-cell communication to cytoskeletal bending is a mechanism read off the histology, without a molecular dataset that would distinguish those subroutines. The anatomical part is partly checkable; the mechanism switch is not.

operationalization: On public pathway maps, score each network for a narrow intermediate layer that many inputs converge on and that many outputs diverge from. A high rate of that topology in biochemical, bioelectric, and biomechanical maps would support the claim; restriction to a few metabolic networks would refute the claim that the architecture is common across those classes.

candidate_datasets.name: Reactome
candidate_datasets.role: curated reaction maps whose input-intermediate-output structure can be scored for hourglass topology

candidate_datasets.name: KEGG
candidate_datasets.role: pathway maps for a second, independently curated count of bowtie architectures in metabolism and signalling

obstacles: Formal definitions of a bowtie disagree on how narrow the waist must be.
Bioelectric and biomechanical processes are poorly represented relative to metabolic pathways.
The egg-stage and learning cases are not in these pathway databases.
rationale: Biochemical pathway databases are public and can be scored, with standard graph methods, for an hourglass or bowtie shape. That covers only part of the stated scope: bioelectrical and biomechanical pathways are sparsely mapped, and the claim also includes the egg stage and learning. Competing definitions of the waist make the test informative but not clean, so the claim is only partly resolvable.

operationalization: Regulative versus mosaic development can be ranked from embryological experiments, but no result would show that the ranking is a willingness to confabulate rather than a difference in developmental constraint.
obstacles: Confabulation in anatomical space has no measure distinct from regulative capacity.
The spectrum from C. elegans to planaria mixes developmental mode, genome, and regenerative ecology.
rationale: The plasticity ordering itself is a familiar comparative description. The proposed underlying parameter, willingness to confabulate and to discount genetic priors, does not name an observation that would come out differently from ordinary differences in mosaic versus regulative development. The claim is a reinterpretation, not a separable empirical statement.

operationalization: Quantify planarian genome heterozygosity, repeat content, and ploidy variation from public assemblies, and set those beside published rates of regeneration, tumor formation, and actuarial aging. The pattern-completion cause would further require re-running the cited evolutionary simulation and showing that disabling pattern completion removes the resistance.

candidate_datasets.name: PlanMine
candidate_datasets.role: Schmidtea mediterranea assemblies and annotations for assessing genome fragmentation, heterozygosity, and repeat load

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Genome
candidate_datasets.role: public planarian genome assemblies used to check how disordered the genome is relative to other metazoans

obstacles: The pattern-completion simulation is not a clearly reusable public code base.
Cancer resistance and negligible senescence are not quantified in one cohort dataset.
A noisy genome co-occurring with regeneration does not show that pattern completion is the cause.
rationale: Public assemblies can test the noisy-genome half, and the regeneration literature is large, so that portion of the statement is partly checkable. Tumor resistance and lack of aging are not settled by a public longitudinal dataset, and the causal appeal to an in silico pattern-completion strategy cannot be rerun from a deposited model. Genomic data alone do not discriminate that mechanism from other explanations of planarian robustness.

operationalization: Across metazoan genomes, rank repeat content, heterozygosity, and assembly difficulty against independent scores of regenerative completeness and cancer incidence. A positive relationship would fit the suggestion; a negative or null relationship would count against it. The historical because-of claim still needs a design that separates cause from correlate.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Genome
candidate_datasets.role: comparative assemblies for ranking genomic repetitiveness and heterozygosity against regenerative taxa

candidate_datasets.name: PlanMine
candidate_datasets.role: planarian genome features used as the extreme case of a noisy genome with high regenerative capacity

obstacles: Regeneration and cancer incidence are not coded in the genome databases.
A cross-species correlation cannot show that intelligence arose because of substrate noise.
Planaria are one clade, so they cannot establish a general evolutionary cause.
rationale: Genome repositories make the noise side of the comparison measurable, and regeneration can be compiled from the literature for a coarse test of co-occurrence. That is only a proxy for a historical causal claim. Many life-history and phylogenetic confounds remain, and no existing dataset records the evolutionary counterfactual the claim requires.

operationalization: Compare evolutionary rates of genes that implement physiological compensation, such as ion channels and gap-junction components, with rates of structural and housekeeping genes, across multicellular phylogenies. Faster evolution of the competency class would be consistent with the ratchet; equal or slower rates would weaken it. Blindness of selection and positive feedback are not identified by the rate comparison alone.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Genome
candidate_datasets.role: coding sequences for a coarse dN/dS comparison of physiological-control genes and structural genes

obstacles: Competency mechanism is not a gene class that genomes label.
Rate differences have many causes besides selection failing to see defects.
The ratchet itself is an evolutionary model without a public run that isolates the feedback loop.
rationale: Public coding sequences support a weak proxy, a comparison of substitution rates between putative control genes and structural genes. They do not record whether selection can see genome quality, nor whether change preferentially accumulates in competency mechanisms because of a feedback ratchet. The historical mechanism stays underdetermined by the sequence data.

operationalization: After a defined training stimulus, test whether the changed response persists when synaptic transmission, intrinsic excitability, or non-neural cell state is disrupted one at a time. Persistence after synaptic disruption would refute a synapse-only substrate; showing that some component classes cannot store the change would refute the claim that every component can serve as a scratchpad.
obstacles: Evidence for non-synaptic and non-neural memory is scattered across literatures and is not one dataset.
A universal quantifier over every component cannot be confirmed by a finite set of substrates.
Training protocols and readouts are not comparable across synapses, epigenomes, and tissues.
rationale: Published work on intrinsic excitability, epigenetic persistence, and behavior after loss of brain tissue can challenge the rival that engrams reside only in synapses. That is a partial test, and the studies would have to be compiled by hand. The positive claim that there is no privileged substrate and that every component can be used as a scratchpad is stronger than those cases and is not covered by any existing dataset.

operationalization: Train published gene-regulatory network models on an associative conditioning protocol without rewiring them, and compare an integration measure before and after training against untrained and random-network controls. A reliable increase supports the network prediction; no increase, or an equal increase in untrained controls, refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: IntegratedInformationGeneRegulation
candidate_datasets.role: public code that trains gene-regulatory models on associative conditioning and recomputes causal emergence

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: deposited dynamical models of biological networks used as the training substrates

obstacles: Causal emergence is one operationalization of integrated information and need not match other phi-style measures.
The code covers network models, not a rat's lever-reward memory or a collective Self.
Results depend on the training schedule and on how network state is coarse-grained.
rationale: The gene-network half of the proposal is now a re-runnable analysis: public code applies associative training to deposited biological models and scores causal emergence against random controls. That does not cover the behavioral example or the claim about reifying a collective Self, and a different integration measure could disagree. The testable network prediction is in good shape; the full statement is only partly resolved by it.

operationalization: Uncertainty about memory could be proxied by metacognitive or physiological measures, but those measures would not distinguish this hypothesis from other theories that tie consciousness to uncertainty, prediction error, or internal monitoring.
obstacles: Consciousness has no agreed measurement that would uniquely confirm this extension of Solms.
Palpated uncertainty about memories is not separable from ordinary metacognition or recall failure.
rationale: The statement is a hypothesis about what consciousness is. Neural and behavioral correlates of uncertainty can be recorded, and they remain compatible with several rival theories. No existing dataset contains an observation that would confirm or refute this identification.

operationalization: Phylogenies can order the appearance of multicellular development and of nervous systems, but that order does not distinguish derivation of behavioral intelligence from morphogenetic problem-solving from other accounts of how behavior evolved.
obstacles: Morphogenetic problem-solving competency is not a character coded in comparative datasets.
Earlier appearance of development than of brains is predicted by many evolutionary stories.
The cause cited, inevitability of mutation and injury, is not a separate observable.
rationale: Comparative biology can show that anatomical development precedes nervous systems. That fact does not test the specific historical claim that behavioral intelligence evolved from morphogenetic competencies. Fossils and genomes lack a variable that would separate this origin story from its rivals, so the claim is not empirically resolvable with current data.

operationalization: From public assemblies, measure heterozygosity, repeats, and ploidy variation in asexual Schmidtea, and compile regeneration success, tumor incidence under defined challenges, and survival curves. High genomic disorder together with high regeneration, low tumor incidence, and no actuarial aging would support the generalization; a stable diploid genome, poor regeneration, or a clear aging curve in the asexual strain would refute the corresponding clause.

candidate_datasets.name: PlanMine
candidate_datasets.role: assemblies and expression resources for the asexual and sexual Schmidtea genomes

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Genome
candidate_datasets.role: deposited planarian genome sequences used to assess polymorphism, repeats, and assembly contiguity

obstacles: Lifespan and tumor-incidence numbers are not in the genome databases and are sparse for asexual strains.
Sexual Schmidtea aging data do not directly cover the asexual animals named in the claim.
Champions of regeneration is a comparative ranking without a single coded trait matrix.
rationale: Genome disorder and regenerative capacity are the parts of the claim that public sequence resources and the regeneration literature can actually address. Cancer resistance and absence of aging are not in a systematic open cohort, and published carcinogenesis and sexual-strain aging studies already show that the absolute wording needs a narrower reading. The generalization is checkable in pieces, not as a single analysis.

operationalization: Match interventions that set a tissue-level target, using stimuli, training, or physiological setpoints, against interventions that manipulate the same outcome by editing individual molecular parts, and compare effect size, durability, and off-target cost. A consistent advantage for the first class would support the therapeutic claim; no advantage would refute it.
obstacles: No public trial or experimental archive is structured as behavior-level versus molecular micromanagement.
Collective intelligence in anatomical space is not a covariate in clinical outcome datasets.
Published case studies use incommensurable endpoints and are mostly preclinical.
rationale: The therapeutic prediction can be stated as a comparison of outcomes, so it is testable in principle. Existing papers report individual bioelectric or training interventions, but they are not a dataset that contrasts those approaches with biochemical micromanagement across indications. Settling the general claim requires that comparative evidence, which is not publicly available.

operationalization: The text defines intelligence as reaching the same goal by different means. A definition is not confirmed or refuted by observing that some systems do so.
obstacles: The claim states a definition rather than an empirical generalization.
Goal and different means become empirical only after a further operational choice the definition does not fix.
rationale: William James's formulation is adopted here as the meaning of intelligence, including for morphogenesis. Data can show that a tissue reaches one anatomy by more than one route, and that result illustrates the definition rather than testing it. The claim has no empirical truth condition.

operationalization: Apply habituation, sensitization, and Pavlovian pairing protocols to published gene-regulatory and pathway models while freezing topology and edge weights, and test the trained response against unpaired and random-network controls. The three learning signatures without parameter change would confirm the claim; failure to obtain them under the published protocols would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: public MATLAB implementation of continuous gene-regulatory and pathway models trained for habituation, sensitization, and associative conditioning

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: deposited pathway and gene-regulatory models on which the same fixed-topology training protocols can be rerun

obstacles: The original Boolean implementation was not released, so the rerun uses the published protocol and the later public ODE code.
Learning labels depend on stimulus timing and on which nodes are treated as cue and response.
rationale: The claim is a simulation result about a defined class of models, and the training rules are specified well enough to reimplement. A public repository already runs habituation, sensitization, and associative conditioning on continuous biological networks without rewiring, and deposited pathway models supply further substrates. A small team can rerun those protocols in weeks, which is enough to confirm or refute the claim as a result about these models.

operationalization: Reanalyze the deposited head transcriptomes of barium-adapted versus control Dugesia and count genes that pass a pre-specified false-discovery threshold, then set that count beside the published head-loss and regeneration observations. A large coherent expression program would refute the handful-of-genes clause; a very small set would support it. The RNA-seq does not itself show that the new heads are morphologically normal or that no evolved barium response exists.

candidate_datasets.name: Gene Expression Omnibus GSE98084
candidate_datasets.role: Dugesia japonica RNA-seq of barium-adapted versus control regenerated heads, for counting differentially expressed genes

obstacles: Head degeneration and morphological normality are not in the expression deposit.
One species and one lab's regeneration series limit the scope.
A small gene list is still compatible with an evolved ion-homeostasis response rather than an improvised solution.
rationale: The transcriptomic clause is directly reanalyzable: GSE98084 contains the adapted-head and control libraries, so the number of differentially expressed genes can be counted without new experiments. The anatomical claims, complete adaptation and absence of an evolved barium program, are not variables in that matrix and remain tied to one group's regeneration observations. The expression half can be resolved now; the full statement cannot.

operationalization: Regulative development already records movement from varied starts to a species-typical anatomy. Describing that record as behavior, navigation, or problem-solving does not add an observation that would distinguish it from the anatomical description.
obstacles: The text presents the framing as a useful metaphor.
Competency from random walk to advanced problem-solving has no separate measurement scale in existing anatomical data.
rationale: Arrival at a target morphology from different starting conditions is the familiar content of regulative development. The claim's distinctive content is to treat that process as behavior in morphospace and as a reason to import cognitive tools. No public dataset distinguishes that cognitive description from a non-cognitive description of the same morphogenetic facts.

operationalization: After a defined anatomical perturbation, test whether the system reduces an error relative to a species-typical target by alternative molecular routes, or instead follows a fixed sequence that does not depend on the remaining error. Return toward the target by more than one route favors closed-loop homeostasis; a single obligatory sequence favors open-loop development.
obstacles: Perturbation-recovery series are scattered through the embryological literature and are not one dataset.
Error relative to a target can be redescribed as late-acting induction without a stored setpoint.
Nothing currently measures whether a setpoint is a complex data structure rather than a scalar or a gradient.
rationale: Classic regulative experiments are published measurements of recovery after displacement, so the open-loop versus feedback contrast can be examined for particular organs. Those records are not a harmonized dataset, and they do not encode the molecular steps or show that the stored target is a complex data structure. The feedback idea is partly testable; the data-structure clause is not resolved by what is public.

operationalization: Take the IUPHAR ion-channel gene set and test whether Human Phenotype Ontology and ClinVar annotations for structural malformations are enriched relative to frequency-matched non-channel genes. Enrichment would support the channelopathy-patterning clause; no enrichment would refute it. Applicability of drugs, optogenetics, and training to morphogenesis is a separate experimental question those databases do not contain.

candidate_datasets.name: Human Phenotype Ontology
candidate_datasets.role: structured human phenotype annotations linking genes, including ion channels, to developmental and craniofacial abnormalities

candidate_datasets.name: ClinVar
candidate_datasets.role: public variant-condition records used to count channel mutations that co-occur with patterning phenotypes

candidate_datasets.name: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology
candidate_datasets.role: curated catalogue of ion-channel genes used as the denominator for an enrichment test

obstacles: Channel genes are heavily sequenced, so phenotype enrichment can be an ascertainment artifact.
Human clinical terms only partly cover the vertebrate developmental scope.
The databases do not record whether neuroscience tools alter morphogenetic decisions.
rationale: The channelopathy half can be tested now with standard enrichment methods on public gene, variant, and phenotype resources. Ascertainment bias and the breadth of malformation terms keep that test from being clean, and it says nothing about optogenetics or training protocols applied to morphogenesis. The symmetry claim is therefore only partly resolvable from data that exist today.

operationalization: Map resting potential across the embryonic face, predict regional gene expression and craniofacial anatomy from that map, and then shift the map by pharmacology, optogenetics, or channel misexpression. Anatomy and markers should follow the imposed pattern if the claim is right, and should ignore it if voltage is only a correlate.
obstacles: Face-wide voltage images, marker domains, and craniofacial outcomes are not in a public deposit.
Human channelopathy phenotypes do not include the embryonic voltage map the mechanism requires.
The manipulation series is largely from one research program and lacks an open independent replicate.
rationale: The electric-face claim has a clear experimental signature: spatial voltage, the expression pattern it is said to set, and the anatomical result of changing it. Those paired measurements were published as figures and are not available as analyzable raw data, and clinical phenotype databases do not contain the voltage variable. Confirming or refuting the result requires the deposited or independently replicated maps, which are not public.

operationalization: Misexpress potassium channels in Xenopus blastomeres outside the anterior neural field and score eye structures by location, including gut and tail, against lineage-tracer and Pax6-only controls. Eyes in posterior tissues after a voltage change, and not after the tracer alone, would support the claim; restriction of eyes to the anterior neural field would refute it.
obstacles: Embryo-level locations and histological scores are published as summaries, not as a public table.
There is no independent open replication dataset.
Pax6 expression atlases do not record the voltage perturbation.
rationale: Eye location after a specified channel misexpression is a standard, countable outcome, and the original paper reports percentages and body positions. Those embryo scores are not deposited, and public gene-expression resources for Pax6 do not contain the voltage experiment needed to compare competence. An outside reanalysis cannot confirm or refute the result without the raw series or a new experiment.

operationalization: Count ectopic eye spots per embryo over stages in channel-injected Xenopus, and record whether final eye number is one. A spot-count trajectory alone cannot separate competing setpoints from lateral inhibition unless signalling between injected and uninjected neighbors is also measured in both directions.
obstacles: Stage-wise spot counts are not a public dataset.
Bidirectional signalling between eye-biased and gut-biased cells was not deposited as a measurement.
A decline from many spots to one eye is also predicted by competition and lateral inhibition without goals.
rationale: The numerical pattern, many early spots and usually one later eye, would be checkable if the counts were public, and they are not. Even those counts would not discriminate competing morphogenetic goals from ordinary neighbor competition, because both predict pruning of extra foci. The mechanism as stated needs new measurements of the proposed bidirectional signals.

operationalization: In frog embryos exposed to alcohol, nicotine, or a dominant Notch construct, compare brain morphology, neural-plate markers, and a learning assay with and without forced restoration of the normal voltage prepattern, for example by HCN2. Rescue on all three readouts would support the claim; restoration of voltage without rescue, or rescue without voltage normalization, would refute it.
obstacles: Morphology scores, in situ results, and learning performance are not in a public archive.
The three teratogens and the Notch model are separate experiments and would have to be reanalyzed together.
No independent open replication covers the rescue design.
rationale: The rescue design is explicit: teratogen or Notch disruption, a voltage-prepattern measurement, and morphological, molecular, and behavioral endpoints. Those data are in the original experimental reports rather than a repository that can be reanalyzed. Public expression atlases do not include the HCN2-rescue contrast, so the claim waits on data that are not currently available.

operationalization: The spatial scale of tissue-level homeostasis can be measured, but a smaller homeostatic domain does not distinguish smaller selves from loss of coupling, and it does not decide whether cells are less selfish.
obstacles: Self size and selfishness are not separately measurable in tumor data.
Any isolation phenotype can be described either as a smaller self or as failed multicellular control.
rationale: The cognitive-light-cone wording restates cancer as a retreat from tissue-scale goals to cell-scale goals. Gap-junction loss, autonomous proliferation, and disregard of tissue boundaries are the same facts under a non-cognitive description. No existing observation would show that cancer cells are not more selfish but instead have smaller selves.

operationalization: In early transformation, measure gap-junction coupling over time and test whether an experimental reduction in coupling raises the probability of further uncoupling and of local, rather than tissue-scale, growth control. A rising hazard of further closure after partial uncoupling would support the feedback claim; independent closures, or no link to loss of tissue-level anatomy, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Genomic Data Commons
candidate_datasets.role: tumor versus normal expression of connexin and other gap-junction genes as a static proxy for physiological isolation

obstacles: Expression of junction genes is not junction permeability, and tumors are sampled once.
A cross-sectional expression difference cannot show positive feedback.
Geometric-barrier tumor experiments are not in cancer genomics archives.
rationale: Cancer genomics can show whether gap-junction transcripts are lower in tumors, which is a weak correlate of the isolation half of the claim. The claim's distinctive content is a positive feedback loop in which each loss of coupling makes the next loss more likely, and a one-time expression matrix cannot test that sequence. The feedback mechanism remains only partly addressable with public data.

operationalization: In embryos expressing human oncogenes, compare the earliest membrane-voltage deviation with later tumor formation, against voltage-matched non-oncogene controls. Detection of a voltage anomaly before overt tumor, with usable sensitivity and specificity, would support the claim; voltage changes only after a tumor is visible, or no voltage change, would refute it.
obstacles: The voltage images and tumor scores are not publicly deposited.
Standard cancer imaging archives do not include embryonic membrane-voltage channels.
The result is from one experimental system without an open independent replicate.
rationale: Early detection by voltage imaging is a defined classification problem with a time order. The Xenopus oncogene experiments that report it do not have a public image and label set, and clinical imaging collections do not measure resting potential in that system. The result cannot be confirmed or refuted by analysis of data that are currently open.

operationalization: Transiently perturb bioelectric and serotonergic signalling in Xenopus melanocytes, then score a pre-specified melanoma-like phenotype against controls that lack carcinogen, oncogene, and detectable DNA damage. Induction by the transient perturbation alone would support the claim; dependence on DNA damage or an oncogene would refute it.
obstacles: Phenotype counts, serotonin manipulations, and DNA-damage controls are not in a public dataset.
Melanoma genomics resources are human tumors, not this embryonic conversion assay.
Melanoma-like needs a fixed histological criterion to avoid circular scoring.
rationale: The experiment is operational: a short physiological perturbation, explicit negative controls for the usual carcinogenic causes, and a pigment-cell phenotype. Those measurements were reported by the originating studies and were not deposited as analyzable counts or images. Human tumor archives do not contain the transient-perturbation design, so the claim needs data that are not yet public.

operationalization: Express a human oncogene such as KRAS in Xenopus and compare tumor incidence and normalization when membrane voltage is forced toward the normal hyperpolarized state, without altering the oncogene. Fewer or normalized tumors only in the voltage-rescued arm would support the claim; no effect of voltage, or rescue only when the oncogene is removed, would refute it.
obstacles: Incidence tables for oncogene-only versus oncogene-plus-hyperpolarization arms are not deposited.
Cancer genomic portals record mutations, not a bioelectric intervention with the mutation left in place.
The rescue series has no public independent replicate.
rationale: Preventing or normalizing an oncogene-driven tumor by a voltage intervention, while leaving the oncogene in place, is a clean contrast. The published Xenopus experiments are not accompanied by a public animal-level dataset, and human cancer resources lack the bioelectric treatment arm. The result cannot be reanalyzed from open data.

operationalization: Partition tumor outcome variance between measured bioelectric connectivity and genotype in the same subjects, or compare normalization by restoring connectivity against normalization by correcting the oncogene. Physiological variables explaining more outcome than genotype would support dominance; the reverse would refute it.
obstacles: Public cancer cohorts measure mutations and expression, not tissue-scale bioelectric state.
The Xenopus rescue experiments are not a deposited dataset and do not cover clinical outcomes.
Dominance is a quantitative comparison that a narrative reading of either literature cannot settle.
rationale: The dominance claim is testable once bioelectric state and genotype are measured on the same outcomes, but no public resource contains both. Genomic cancer archives can describe genetic associations and cannot show that physiological information processing outweighs them. The frog intervention papers do not fill that gap as open data, so the claim needs new or newly deposited measurements.

operationalization: Reanalyze RNA-seq from large versus small Xenopus cohorts, with and without teratogen, and test for a cohort-size-specific expression signature. Separately, morphological protection would be scored as the rate of teratogen-induced defects in large versus small groups. A distinct large-group transcriptome and a lower defect rate would support the claim; no expression difference and no survival advantage would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Gene Expression Omnibus GSE245782
candidate_datasets.role: Xenopus RNA-seq of small versus large embryo groups with and without thioridazine, at two stages

obstacles: The deposit is one species and one teratogen, thioridazine.
Defect and survival rates are not in the expression matrix.
A modest gene list may be a group-size effect without establishing a hyperembryo that resists teratogens far better.
rationale: GSE245782 is an open test of the transcriptome clause: large versus small groups, treated and untreated, at two stages, can be reanalyzed with ordinary differential-expression methods. The claim also says large groups resist teratogens far better than individuals or small groups, and that morphological outcome is not in the sequence archive. Expression can be resolved now; the resistance half cannot.

operationalization: Deliver the same systemic monensin treatment to animals with either a tail wound or a leg wound and score regenerate identity. Tails at tail wounds and legs at leg wounds would support specificity in the responding collective; identical structures at both sites, or no regeneration, would refute it.
obstacles: Published tail regeneration indices are not a deposited animal-level dataset.
The froglet limb series is not available as public raw counts or an independent replication.
Systemic exposure has to be matched so that site differences are not dose differences.
rationale: Site-appropriate regeneration after one drug is a direct anatomical comparison, and tail experiments have published summary indices. The paired tail-versus-leg scores required by the claim are not in a public file, and the limb result has not been released as an analyzable replicate set. Checking specificity in the cell collective requires those data.

operationalization: Track tissue-scale resting-potential patterns in the same animals as they age, alongside cell-intrinsic aging markers, and test whether restoring the voltage pattern preserves tissue order when cell-level rejuvenation is held constant. Pattern decay predicting disorder, and pattern restoration preventing it, would support the claim; aging with an intact voltage pattern, or rescue by cell-level factors alone, would refute it.
obstacles: No public longitudinal dataset pairs bioelectric prepatterns with tissue order across age.
Aging clocks and expression atlases do not record membrane-voltage pattern memory.
Pattern memory has to be specified so that ordinary loss of cell function is not counted as evidence.
rationale: The aging hypothesis can be turned into a longitudinal contrast between voltage-pattern stability and cell-intrinsic aging markers, with a restoration test. Public aging resources contain molecular and clinical clocks and do not contain the endogenous bioelectric patterns the claim treats as the information scaffold. The necessary paired measurements are not available for analysis.
